name: Cheltenham Half Marathon
notes: The A race. Target 1:21-1:23, model predicts 1:22:23. COURSE (from a clubmate's 2025 file — her run, not his — who ran 1:21:02, so her splits map the course at almost exactly his goal pace): 101m gain over 21.09km, ~4.8m/km, rolling rather than flat, net slightly downhill start to finish. Her watch had no barometric altimeter, so treat the metres as approximate and the shape as the signal. Km 1 is downhill and her fastest of the day (3:38) — the start is a trap. Highest ground is the first 8km, which roll continuously. Flattest running is roughly 14-18km. The sting is km 19-20: a climb of about 11m that produced her slowest split of the race (4:11, seven seconds off anything else), immediately followed by a 6m drop to the line where she ran 3:54. Expect the 20km split to look bad and the last km to be free. HER PACING IS THE WARNING: first 10km 37:08 (3:43/km), second 10km 39:33 (3:57/km) — 2:25 lost in the back half after going out 7 sec/km faster than her own average. 3:43/km is Shep's current 10K race pace, so running with that early group means racing a half at 10K pace.

name: Crete 10K
notes: Fun race with beers on the way over. Falls in the HM recovery window, which is fine — no taper.

name: Guy Fawkes 5
notes: 5 miles, and the first race he actually races after Cheltenham. Club record 29:12. Riegel off Cheltenham (1:21:04, 20 Sep 2026) projects 29:11 — one second inside, where the pre-race projection off Jun/Jul data said 29:40. Level, not banked: Riegel's error bars are wider than a second. THE RUN-IN IS NOW CLEAR AND DELIBERATE: he cancelled the 18 Oct XC on 20 Sep to make it so, having already dropped 31 Oct. Nothing hard sits in the four weeks before this except Crete on 4 Oct, which is a fun run with beers and no taper. That leaves ~4 weeks after HM recovery to write as an actual sharpening block — short, fast work at 5-mile pace rather than half-marathon volume — which is what the record needs and what was missing when it read 29:40. He has paid the XC league for this; do not let the block drift back into general aerobic work. Recompute from race_prediction.json once Cheltenham is logged.

name: Manchester Marathon
notes: Goal sub-3 (4:16/km). Volume, not fitness, is the binding constraint — and Cheltenham widened that gap rather than closing it: 1:21:04 projects a 2:49 marathon, against 2:52 before. The fitness is comfortably there on paper; what is missing is that he has never run one, his longest run ever is ~29 km, and carbohydrate at marathon pace in marathon quantity is untested.
